books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

stimulus.source_note: Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, February 2, 1848, Articles IX and XII (ratified text). Public domain.
stimulus.text: The Mexicans who, in the territories aforesaid, shall not preserve the character of citizens of the Mexican Republic... shall be incorporated into the Union of the United States, and be admitted at the proper time (to be judged of by the Congress of the United States) to the enjoyment of all the rights of citizens of the United States... In consideration of the extension acquired by the boundaries of the United States, as defined in the fifth article of the present treaty, the Government of the United States engages to pay to that of the Mexican Republic the sum of fifteen millions of dollars.

source: original; stimulus is a verbatim excerpt from the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, February 2, 1848, Articles IX and XII, public domain
stem: According to the treaty, the United States agreed to pay Mexico how much for the ceded territory?

options.misconception: $3 million was the first installment, paid at ratification, not the total.
$25 million was the sum offered for California alone during the Slidell mission, not the treaty price.
$5 million was the price of Florida in 1819, not the Mexican Cession.

rationales.A: Article XII says the United States “engages to pay to that of the Mexican Republic the sum of fifteen millions of dollars.”
rationales.B: Three million dollars was the first payment, made at ratification; the total was fifteen million.
rationales.C: Twenty-five million dollars was offered for California during the Slidell mission in 1845, not the price in the treaty.
rationales.D: Five million dollars was the price of Florida in 1819, not of the Mexican Cession.
rationales.general:
1. Find the payment sentence. Article XII says the United States will pay “the sum of fifteen millions of dollars.”
2. Keep the installments straight. Three million came at ratification, and twelve million more followed in yearly installments.
3. Do not borrow other prices. Twenty-five million was an earlier offer for California, and five million was Florida.
Remember: a total and its first payment are different numbers. The treaty names both — read which one the question asks for.
